s1.syndrome_frame: Congenital skin lesion with atrophic plaque and vascular features
salient_findings: Congenital skin lesion on the left supraclavicular area
Dark brown atrophic plaque with a linear midline depression
Elevated, compressible, soft border paler than the central portion
Visible small vein within the plaque
Extensive network of small superficial branching vessels
key_facts: 5-month-old dark-skinned boy
Lesion present at birth
Lesion measured 11 cm × 3.5 cm at birth
Lesion measured 10 cm × 2.5 cm at 5 months
Lesion is nonpulsatile and well-demarcated
Birth and neonatal history were unremarkable
Patient is healthy and not on medications
Small vein (~0.3 mm) visible to the naked eye within the plaque
AccuVein AV400 revealed one large vein with an extensive network of small superficial branching vessels

shortlist.label: Rapidly involuting congenital hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Lesion present at birth, nonpulsatile, and well-demarcated with vascular features

shortlist.label: Congenital hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Lesion present at birth with vascular features and involuting characteristics

shortlist.label: Kasabach-Merritt syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a vascular lesion with potential for thrombocytopenia and coagulopathy

shortlist.label: Tufted angioma
shortlist.why_kept: Vascular lesion with potential for involution and presence of small superficial branching vessels

shortlist.label: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Vascular lesion with potential for involution and presence of small superficial branching vessels

raw.rationale: The lesion was present at birth, nonpulsatile, and had a significant decrease in size from birth to 5 months, which is consistent with the natural history of rapidly involuting congenital hemangioma (RICH). The presence of a large vein with an extensive network of small superficial branching vessels also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Congenital hemangioma
rejected.why: Too broad, as RICH is a specific subtype of congenital hemangioma

rejected.label: Kasabach-Merritt syndrome
rejected.why: Typically associated with severe thrombocytopenia and coagulopathy, which is not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Tufted angioma
rejected.why: Usually presents with a distinctive clinical appearance of a reddish-brown plaque with a pebbly surface, which is not described in the vignette

rejected.label: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma
rejected.why: Typically presents with a more aggressive clinical course and is often associated with Kasabach-Merritt syndrome, which is not consistent with the vignette
